module purpose: neorv32_fifo buffers input data words in a one-entry or deeper FIFO, updates read/write position state on qualified write and read events, and returns the selected stored word on rdata_o. It also computes and exports occupancy and threshold status through level_o, free_o, avail_o, and half_o, with optional safe qualification and optional registered read/status outputs.

use-case flows.value: qualified write acceptance, optionally masked by free when FIFO_SAFE is true
qualified read acceptance, optionally masked by avail when FIFO_SAFE is true
write data stored into the one-entry register or indexed memory and pointer state advanced
selected stored data word driven on rdata_o through the asynchronous or synchronous read path
occupancy and threshold status derived from the pointers and exported on level_o, free_o, avail_o, and half_o
pointer state forced to zero by rstn_i or clear_i, with optional storage reset and registered status reset

conceptual assets.concept: Qualified write acceptance decision -- whether an input word is accepted into FIFO storage on this cycle
conceptual assets.reasoning: The write-start flow computes `we` from `we_i` and, when FIFO_SAFE is true, `free` (line 65). That decision alone enables write-pointer advance in `w_nxt` (line 82) and the actual stores inside the `if (we = '1')` arms for fifo_reg and fifo_mem (lines 134-135, 149-150, 170-171, 183-184). Integrity is established because accepting a write outside this predicate would advance the FIFO state or overwrite storage incorrectly; availability is established because the RTL performs the write update when the predicate holds at a rising edge.

conceptual assets.concept: Qualified read acceptance decision -- whether the FIFO advances to the next read position on this cycle
conceptual assets.reasoning: The read-start flow computes `re` from `re_i` and, when FIFO_SAFE is true, `avail` (line 64). That decision controls read-pointer advance in `r_nxt` (line 83); the updated pointer is stored at line 77 and is then used by the read-data selection path through `r_pnt_ff` or `r_pnt` (lines 210, 213, 241). Integrity is established because only qualified reads should advance the read position selected by the RTL; availability is established because the design progresses the read state when the predicate holds at a rising edge.

conceptual assets.concept: Buffered payload data -- write-side data values held in FIFO storage and delivered at the read-data output
conceptual assets.reasoning: The operate and read-out flows store incoming data into `fifo_reg` for depth 1 or `fifo_mem` for depth greater than 1 (`fifo_reg <= wdata_i` at lines 135 and 171; `fifo_mem(...) <= wdata_i` at lines 150 and 184), and expose a selected stored word on `rdata_o` by copying `fifo_reg` (lines 201 and 232) or deriving from `fifo_mem` (lines 213 and 241). Integrity is established because the consumer of `rdata_o` must receive exactly the stored word selected by the implemented read path; availability is established because the RTL provides both storage and an output path for the buffered word under the selected configuration.

conceptual assets.concept: FIFO occupancy and ordering state -- the held read and write positions that determine where data is stored, where it is read from, and whether the FIFO is empty or full
conceptual assets.reasoning: `w_pnt` and `r_pnt` are reset to zero at lines 73-74 and updated from `w_nxt` and `r_nxt` at lines 76-77; `clear_i` forces the next pointer values to zero at lines 82-83. This state selects write addresses (lines 150 and 184), read addresses (line 241 and, through `r_pnt_ff`, line 213), and the occupancy/status computations at lines 92-95 and 102-105. Integrity is established because corrupt pointer state misaddresses stored data and miscomputes status; availability is established because the state is retained between rising edges and can be cleared or reset by the RTL conditions.

conceptual assets.concept: FIFO fill level count -- the occupancy count reported on level_o
conceptual assets.reasoning: For depth greater than 1, `level` is computed as `unsigned(w_pnt) - unsigned(r_pnt)` (line 95); for depth 1, `level` is filled from `full` (line 105). The output process zero-extends and drives this value on `level_o` at lines 116-117. Integrity is established because the report flow depends on this count being the one defined by the pointer arithmetic; availability is established because `level_o` is continuously driven from `level`.

conceptual assets.concept: Space-available status -- the decision that a further write is permitted
conceptual assets.reasoning: `free` is computed as `not full` at line 110. That status is used locally to qualify writes when FIFO_SAFE is true (`we_i and free`, line 65) and is exported on `free_o` either combinationally (line 217) or in the registered status path (line 254). Integrity is established because the write-start flow and the reported status both depend on this decision having exactly the implemented value; availability is established because the status is driven out in both read-status configurations.

conceptual assets.concept: Data-available status -- the decision that a further read is permitted
conceptual assets.reasoning: `avail` is computed as `not empty` at line 111. That status is used locally to qualify reads when FIFO_SAFE is true (`re_i and avail`, line 64) and is exported on `avail_o` either combinationally (line 218) or in the registered status path (line 255). Integrity is established because the read-start flow and the reported status both depend on this decision having exactly the implemented value; availability is established because the status is driven out in both read-status configurations.

conceptual assets.concept: Half-full threshold status -- the decision that occupancy has reached the half/full threshold
conceptual assets.reasoning: For depth greater than 1, `half` is computed from the fill level and `full` (`level(level'left-1) or full`, line 96); for depth 1, `half <= full` at line 106. The result is exported on `half_o` either combinationally (line 219) or in the registered status path (line 256). Integrity is established because the report flow depends on this threshold decision being the one defined by the RTL; availability is established because the status is driven out in both configurations.
